title: Shan Althaf’s Trinity immortals of 2026 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Ranil Prematilake

Inter-school rugby season 2026 scripted a story of unmatched quality produced by Trinity College Kandy culminating with the second leg of the 80th Bradby Shield encounter on the 25th of July at the Lion’s Den at picturesque Pallekele Rugby Stadium.  Bradby Shield only in its 80th year more importantly stands as the world’s second oldest inter-school rugby fixture between Trinity College Kandy and Royal College Colombo dating back to well over a century. 

Trinity’s fairy tale Bradby triumph of 2024 and the dominant destruction of 2026, had its set of heroes spearheaded by a calm and composed Shan Althaf who finally held aloft the prestigious Shield in his eighth Bradby appearance, five of which were rewarded with player of the match awards. Althaf’s instinct driven deceptive penetrative runs during moments of stagnation made the Trinity side look untouchable and a treat to watch right throughout the season.    

Deputy leaders in Nisith Kumarasinghe and senior prefect Udan Wijekoon made the challenges that much easier. Imposing figures of Achintha Jayasena, Minula Yaddehige, Hamza Abdeen, Kevin Weerakoon, Nahil Jayah, Akash Fernando, Sadeesha Weerawansa, Maduranga De Silva, Prathiv Yainne, Rithika Weragama, Dimath Ambepitiya, Bilal Nazeer, Mukshith Shyam, Misala Perera and Vihanga Indusara now becomes a part of Trinity rugby folklore whilst Aamar Malik, Evin Jayasena, Abdul Malik are thrust with the mantle of guiding the schools rugby cradle to continued success. 

For purposes of record Trinity overcame Thurstan College, Zahira College and, Wesley College before dismantling Royal College to win the President’s Trophy Knockout tournament. What followed was a nine match unbeaten run brushing aside opponents’ with relative ease to add the League title for a second year running before regaining the prize scalp – the Bradby Shield with an 72 -20 aggregate.  

In their quest, the schoolboys travelled to Colombo eleven (11) times during the season and the clinical manner in which the opponents succumbed to the powerful expansive brand of rugby dished out with precision guaranteed a fitting farewell to their guiding force in Principal Rev. Fr. Araliya Jayasundera – an old boy whose eyes were filled with tears at Pallekele on Saturday - A mission accomplished to state the least. Meanwhile fellow masterminds the “TCK Rugby Scrummage” spearheaded by the incomparable Nilantha (NLK) Ratnayake, coaching outfit led by the legendary Fazil Marija and Director of Sports Gihan Samarasekara stood resolutely rejoicing months of hard work and perhaps at the thought of Trinity’s rugby pride being well and truly restored.

title: Police recommend removing Kavadi dance from Devinuwara Perahera over security concerns - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - Police have recommended removing the traditional Kavadi dance performance from the upcoming procession of the historic Sri Utpalawanna Sri Vishnu Maha Devalaya in Devinuwara, citing security concerns.

The procession, featuring the Kavadi dance segment, is scheduled to be held on July 28 as part of the annual Devinuwara Vishnu Devalaya Perahera, which is currently underway.

The recommendation was issued by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Priyantha Weerasooriya and formally communicated to the Basnayake Nilame of the Devalaya today (26) by Matara District Secretary Chandana Thilakarathna.

The decision follows intelligence assessments conducted by the Chief of National Intelligence of the Ministry of Defence, the National Intelligence Service and the Police Special Bureau.

According to the intelligence reports, authorities had received information indicating the possibility of a dispute or controversial situation arising between the event organisers and the dancers.

In a written notification to the Matara District Secretary, the IGP strongly recommended that the Kavadi dance segment be excluded from the procession scheduled for July 28 in the interest of public safety.

Acting on the directive, the District Secretary informed the Basnayake Nilame of the Devalaya today and requested that the recommended measure be implemented.

title: Iran war spreads to Red Sea and Caspian, Gulf quiet as US forgoes strikes - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Reuters - The Iran war broadened over the weekend despite a pause in U.S. strikes, as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast and Iran ‌accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea.

The U.S. military said on Saturday its naval blockade against Iran "remains in full effect" but did not explain why it halted a streak of 13 nights of escalating strikes.

There were also no weekend reports of attacks by Iran on neighbors, similar to its daily rejoinders to the U.S. attacks.

Asked about the pause, a senior official in President Donald Trump's administration said Trump "has always been clear that his preference is diplomacy, but he has shown Iran what will happen if they fail to come to the table in a serious way."

Trump has decided, for now, to back away from plans to ramp up attacks on Iran, ⁠the New York Times said on Saturday, citing two people briefed on the discussion.

The president and his advisers, the newspaper said, have concerns about expanding the conflict, depleting defense stockpiles, alienating Middle East Gulf allies and affecting energy supplies and the global economy.

Vice President JD Vance and Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, both raised concerns about the U.S. munitions stockpile with Trump during a White House meeting on Friday, a U.S. official told CNN.

Operations are "on a hold," a Department of Defense source told the broadcaster on Saturday.

Despite the Gulf lull, Saturday's fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia showed that the war, which has already disrupted energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, could affect a second major shipping route and reignite Yemen's civil war.

Separately, Iran's Foreign Ministry accused Ukraine of attacking an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, saying one sailor was killed and another injured.

The ministry summoned Ukraine's chargé d'affaires in Tehran to protest over an attack it described as "hostile and criminal", state news agency IRNA said.

The Iranian denunciation coincided with comments by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy that Kyiv had ‌noted Russia ⁠was passing on to Iran its satellite observations in the Middle East, to enable it to direct strikes in the region.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group struck sites belonging to Saudi state oil company Aramco in the cities of Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday.

A large column of smoke rose from the direction of the Aramco refinery in Jizan, near the Yemeni border, video on social media verified by Reuters showed. The refinery can process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil daily.

Two Asia-based trading sources said they had been informed of potential damage to fuel ⁠and oil storage sites at Jizan. Aramco (2222.SE) did not respond to requests for comment.

In Yanbu, two missiles aimed at oil installations were intercepted. Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea oil port, has become a key route for Saudi oil skirting the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blockaded.

In Yemen, officials said the air force of the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, which has opposed the Houthis for ⁠more than a decade, struck Houthi sites in the Marib and al-Jawf provinces.

The officials said both sides in Yemen's civil war were mobilising forces along the front.

Saudi Arabia has led an Arab coalition battling the Houthis since the Iran-aligned fighters captured Yemen's capital, Sanaa.

The civil war, in which famine and fighting killed hundreds of thousands, has been paused by a ceasefire since ⁠2022.

But that truce broke down this month, with the Houthis effectively joining the wider war their Iranian allies have waged since being attacked by the United States and Israel five months ago.

The Houthis have declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia over the past week, and Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi said all Saudi oil facilities could be targets.

title: Rainfall expected to increase in southwest from July 28: Met Dept - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - The Meteorology Department has forecast a slight increase in rainfall in the south-western parts of Sri Lanka over the next few days from July 28.

Issuing its general weather forecast for the next 36 hours at 4.00 p.m. yesterday (July 26), the Department said several spells of showers are expected in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and North-Western provinces, as well as in the Galle, Matara, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts.

Mainly dry weather conditions are expected to prevail in other parts of the island during this period.

The Department also warned that strong winds reaching speeds of around 40-50 kmph could occur at times in the western slopes of the Central Hills, Northern and North-Central provinces, and in the Hambantota, Trincomalee and Puttalam districts.

title: No closure of Sri Vijaya Dhamma School in Saudi Arabia - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July 26 (Daily Mirror) - A clarification has been issued rejecting claims that the Sri Vijaya Buddhist Dhamma School in Riyadh was closed on the instructions of Sri Lanka's Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Amir Ajwad, describing the reports as false and based on distorted information.

Athula Kumarasinghe, Founding Member and Principal of the Sri Vijaya Buddhist Dhamma School, said the reports alleging that the Ambassador had taken steps to close the school and hinder Buddhist religious activities were completely untrue.

According to Kumarasinghe, the Sri Lankan Embassy in Riyadh has continuously provided facilities and space for the Dhamma School since its establishment in 2007. He explained that the school's activities were only temporarily suspended for a few months after the Embassy relocated to a new premises with limited space, stressing that this did not amount to the closure of the institution.

He further said that, ahead of the 2026/2027 academic year of the Sri Lanka International School in Riyadh, the Ambassador had approved the allocation of space on both the upper and lower floors of the Embassy building for the Dhamma School despite existing space constraints, and had made the necessary arrangements several months ago.

Kumarasinghe also dismissed claims that Buddhist religious activities had been halted, noting that rehearsals for the 2026 Vesak devotional singing programme were held at the Embassy over a month with the Ambassador's approval and patronage.

He added that the main Vesak celebration was shifted to a larger venue only because the Embassy premises could not accommodate the thousands of Sri Lankans who attended the event. The alternative venue was secured with the intervention of the Ambassador and the approval of the relevant Saudi authorities, he said.

Kumarasinghe requested media organisations that carried the earlier reports to publish the clarification, maintaining that the allegations against the Ambassador were misleading and contrary to the facts.

title: Trump pauses Iran strikes over missile shortages - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
The Telegraph - Donald Trump has paused plans to escalate the war on Iran after being warned that the US is running low on missiles.

For the first time in nearly two weeks, the US president called off strikes on the Islamic Republic over the weekend and has set aside plans to return to major combat operations.

The decision also allows time and space for negotiations with Iran.

Concerns were raised during a White House meeting on Friday night, according to reports.

JD Vance, the vice-president, and General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, were among those who spoke out, the New York Times (NYT) reported.

Officials familiar with the deliberations told US media that concerns over dwindling supplies of air-defence munitions, particularly interceptor missiles needed to defend American bases and regional partners against Iranian ballistic missiles and drones, played a central role in the decision.

Three American soldiers were killed in Jordan last Friday when a ballistic missile slipped through American air defences fending off a barrage of Iranian missiles and drones.

Another soldier was killed in Iraq while trying to make safe a downed Iranian drone.

After 13 straight nights of US attacks on Iran, Mr Trump ordered no more strikes on Friday or Saturday night.

A department of defence source told CNN that operations are “on a hold”.

The pause came as Mr Trump also signalled he believes Tehran may now be prepared to negotiate, though Tehran continues to dig its heels in with demands to retain control of the critical Strait of Hormuz.

On Sunday, the Iranian foreign ministry said that technical and political consultations between the two sides were ongoing via Omani intermediaries. Talks over the strait were, Iran said, productive.

Only on Thursday, Mr Trump said that he was considering “a massive attack” on Iran. He described it as “one bigger than ever before. I am close to making a decision. We are all set for it”.

The Pentagon rushed more forces, weaponry and supplies to the Middle East in recent days to prepare for any escalation.

But the meeting on Friday curbed the president’s efforts.

Since the campaign began, the US has damaged or destroyed an increasing number of railway bridges that civilians use but that also enable Iranian commanders to send supplies to the southern coastal region near the strait.

Officials told the NYT that increased attacks on those kinds of targets, as well as energy facilities and Iran’s nuclear sites, including Pickaxe Mountain, were still under consideration.

US officials stress that military options remain on the table should negotiations fail or were Iran to launch further attacks. However, it represents the clearest indication yet that the White House is searching for an off-ramp after five months of conflict.

There is also growing unease within Mr Trump’s inner circle over the prospect of being drawn into a prolonged regional conflict which has triggered backlash domestically.

CNN reported that close advisers had voiced concerns over both the strategic and political costs of expanding the war, particularly given the strain on US military resources, the loss of lives and uncertainty over whether further strikes would fundamentally alter Iran’s behaviour.

title: Referendum needed on Supreme Court judges’ tenure: Namal - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa said any proposal to extend the tenure of Supreme Court judges should be decided by the people through a referendum.

Addressing a public gathering, Rajapaksa said that if the government considered extending the retirement age of Supreme Court judges a national priority, it should seek public approval through a referendum.

Referring to the proposed constitutional amendment to extend the retirement age of Supreme Court judges, he claimed the government was prioritising the issue despite opposition from legal bodies.

Rajapaksa also alleged that the government had lost the people's trust by failing to fulfil its election promises and by imposing an unfair tax burden amid the rising cost of living.

He claimed that farmers, fishermen, students, businesses and investors were facing hardships due to fertiliser shortages, rising food prices, high taxes and increasing utility costs.

Rajapaksa further criticised the government's handling of crime, alleging that organised criminal activity continued despite repeated assurances from the authorities. He also claimed prisons were becoming overcrowded because of delays in forensic reports and court proceedings.

He urged supporters to strengthen the SLPP at the grassroots level, saying the party aimed to build a modern political movement capable of meeting the aspirations of the country's younger generation.

title: Teachers’ Union slams compulsory Poya Day meeting for principals - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - The Ceylon Teachers' Union (CTU) has strongly condemned the decision to hold a meeting for school principals in the Kandy education zone on a Poya Day (29), with General Secretary Joseph Stalin accusing education authorities of making an unfair decision on behalf of the government.

Speaking to the Daily Mirror, Stalin said the Kandy Zonal Education Director should not have taken such a decision, arguing that government officials organising the programme would receive overtime payments for working on the public holiday, while principals would not receive any such compensation.

"The Zonal Education Director must not take such decisions representing the government. Those organising the programme on the Poya Day will be paid overtime, but principals will not receive any payment. Therefore, it is far more appropriate to hold this meeting on a normal weekday," he said.

The controversy follows a circular issued by Kandy Zonal Education Director D.C.I. Andarage directing all principals, deputy principals and assistant principals in the Kandy education zone to attend a programme titled "A Clean Society" under the national mission "A Clean Culture – A Clean Sri Lanka".

According to the circular, the programme, organised in collaboration with the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption, is scheduled to be held at Kandy Girls' High School from 8.30 a.m. to 2.00 p.m. on July 29, which falls on a Poya Day (29).

Stalin urged the education authorities to reschedule the programme to a working day, saying compulsory participation on a public holiday was unjustified and unfair to school administrators.

title: Baghaei says progress made in Oman talks on Strait of Hormuz
summary: Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei says talks were held with Oman on Friday and Saturday over shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. He said progress has been made.

title: National drowning prevention committee to be formed - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - The Government has taken steps to establish a multi-stakeholder national mechanism for drowning prevention and lifesaving, with a progress review meeting held at the Parliament Complex to strengthen coordination among key agencies.

The meeting, which followed an earlier high-level discussion on the initiative, focused on developing a coordinated national framework to reduce water-related fatalities and improve public safety across Sri Lanka.

The session was co-chaired by Deputy Minister of Defence Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd.), Deputy Minister of Education and Higher Education Dr. Madhura Senevirathna, and Deputy Minister of Youth Affairs Dinindu Saman Hennayake.

Addressing the meeting, Deputy Defence Minister Jayasekara said the growing number of drowning deaths is not only a social concern but also a significant public safety issue. He stressed the need for a structured and sustainable national mechanism, noting that the absence of a coordinated approach continues to pose serious risks.

During the discussions, Deputy Minister Senevirathna proposed incorporating water safety education into the national school curriculum to improve awareness among students from an early age. He said integrating water safety into education would help promote responsible behaviour around rivers, lakes, reservoirs and coastal areas.

Meanwhile, Deputy Minister Hennayake highlighted the role young people can play in supporting lifesaving efforts, proposing structured training programmes to develop a volunteer network capable of assisting professional rescue services.

Following deliberations, participants agreed to establish a multi-stakeholder committee headed by the Sri Lanka Coast Guard, with representation from all relevant government institutions and stakeholder agencies. The committee has been tasked with formulating a practical and sustainable National Mechanism for Drowning Prevention and Lifesaving for implementation across the country.

The meeting was attended by the Chiefs of Staff of the Sri Lanka Army, Navy and Air Force, the Director General of the Sri Lanka Coast Guard, senior officials from the Ministries of Defence, Health, Education, Sports and Youth Affairs, and Tourism, as well as representatives from the Disaster Management Centre, Sri Lanka Police, the Institute of National Security Studies, the Civil Security Department, and the Sri Lanka Life Saving Association.

title: Hotel in Ella fined Rs. 1 Mn for overpricing bottled water - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - The Bandarawela Magistrate's Court has imposed a Rs. 1 million fine on a hotel in the Nafora area of Karandagolla, Ella, after it admitted to selling bottled drinking water above the stipulated maximum retail price, authorities said.

The case was filed by investigation officers of the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) in the Badulla District following a raid conducted on July 10, 2026. During the inspection, officials found that the hotel had been charging customers more than the legally permitted price for bottled water.

When the matter was taken up before the Bandarawela Magistrate's Court, the hotel company pleaded guilty to the charges of violating provisions of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act. The court subsequently ordered the company to pay a fine of Rs. 1,000,000.

The Consumer Affairs Authority urged consumers to report hotels, restaurants, and other businesses that violate consumer protection regulations. Complaints can be made through the CAA's 1977 hotline during official working hours.

title: Police Inspector arrested for alleged drunk driving after two hit-and-run crashes - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - A Chief Inspector of Police attached to the Special Investigation Unit of the Homagama Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Division has been arrested for allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol and fleeing the scene after striking two young women in two separate road accidents, police said.

According to the Meegoda Police, the two incidents occurred between on July 25. The first accident took place near the Meegoda fuel station on High-Level Road, while the second occurred near the 20th Mile Post in Wataraka.

Police said the officer allegedly attempted to leave the area in his car after the collisions but was later apprehended by Meegoda Police officers.

A breathalyzer test conducted following the arrest confirmed that the suspect had been driving under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incidents, police said.

The arrested officer, who serves as the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Special Investigation Unit in the Homagama SSP Division, is scheduled to be produced before the Homagama Magistrate's Court today (July 26) for further legal proceedings.

title: Sub-Inspector suspended over misconduct and aggressive behavior - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - A Sub-Inspector attached to the Wathupitiwala Investment Zone Police Post has been suspended with immediate effect following an incident involving inappropriate conduct and threatening behavior toward members of the public.

The incident took place at around on July 23, 2026, in front of a private establishment near the Wathupitiwala Hospital. While in uniform, the officer allegedly engaged in a heated, threatening argument with bystanders, behaving in a manner deemed entirely unbecoming of a duty-bound officer.

Police said that the suspension was executed immediately in accordance with the provisions of the Establishments Code. Official statements emphasized that the officer's actions brought disrepute to both the Sri Lanka Police and the broader public service, set a poor precedent for fellow officers, and tarnished the integrity and dignity of the service.

title: Rescuers scour South China Sea for 23 missing after Vietnamese vessel sinks
summary: Rescuers were searching on Sunday for 23 people missing after a Vietnamese ship sank in the busy waterway of the ‌South China Sea, while 39 were pulled from the waters, China’s state broadcaster CCTV said.

title: Two arrested over Bellanwila shooting - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - Two suspects have been arrested in connection with the fatal shooting of a man in Bellanwila, Boralesgamuwa last night.

The shooting occurred last night when an unidentified gunman opened fire on the victim. He was rushed to the Colombo South Teaching Hospital in Kalubowila, where he later succumbed to his injuries.

Following the incident, a team of officers from the Navagamuwa Police intercepted two suspects in the Ranala area while they were allegedly attempting to flee on a motorcycle believed to have been used in the escape.

Police said 6 grams and 600 milligrams of heroin were recovered from the suspects during the arrest, and the motorcycle was taken into custody.

The suspects, identified as residents of the Bakamuna area aged 28 and 37. The Navagamuwa Police are conducting further inquiries to identify other individuals connected to the incident.
